ASAD-NOTES:53:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:intro/r2.claim: Some passages, especially 53:13–18, belong to a later period and allude to Muhammad's heavenly ascension about a year before the migration to Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:53:intro/r2.anchor: However, some parts of it undoubtedly belong to a later period

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r1.claim: The Prophet saw the angel in the higher horizon and again near the farthest lote-tree; Islahi says this could not be a product of fancy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r1.anchor: There is absolutely no possibility that this observation which he has stated to them be a product of his fancy

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r16.speaker: ابن مسعود، عائشة، مجاهد، الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r16.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, ʿĀʾisha, Mujāhid, and al-Rabīʿ take the object pronoun in “he saw him” to refer to Gabriel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r16.anchor: ولقد رآه: الضمير المنصوب عائد على جبريل عليه السلام، قال ابن مسعود وعائشة ومجاهد والربيع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r18.speaker: ابن عباس، كعب الأحبار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār instead take the object pronoun to refer to God, consistently with their view that Muḥammad saw God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11#2/r18.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وكعب الأحبار: الضمير عائد على الله، على ما سبق من قولهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r1.claim: The Prophet saw his Lord twice.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r2.claim: He parses نزلة as an adverbial accusative, with مرة denoting one occurrence of the action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نصب الظرف الذي هو مرة، لأن الفعلة اسم للمرة من الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r3.speaker: الحوفي وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r3.claim: They parse نزلة as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r3.anchor: وقال الحوفي وابن عطية: مصدر في موضع الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r4.claim: He treats نزلة as a verbal noun meaning another time or another vision.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: مصدر، أي مرة أخرى، أو رؤية أخرى

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.claim: Verses 13–18 refer to the Ascension and may belong to a later period than the early Makkan setting.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.anchor: Vv. 13–18, which refer to the Ascension of the Prophet, may, however, be from a later period

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.claim: Many commentators date the Ascension to the late Makkan period, most likely 619.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.anchor:
many commentators maintain that the Ascension of the Prophet Muhammad (miʿrāj
) did not occur until the late Makkan period, most likely in the year 619

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.speaker: a minority
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.claim: A minority dates the Ascension to 614, seven years before the hijrah.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.anchor: a minority maintain that it occurred seven years before the hijrah in 614

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel another time at the Lote Tree of the Boundary.
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.anchor: أي رآه مرة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#2/r2.claim: Rāzī also reads the statement as emphasis: even a certain person may still face doubts he cannot answer, but inability to answer does not undo certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#2/r2.anchor: وذلك لأن من تيقن شيئا قد يكون بحيث لا يزول عن نفسه تشكيك

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.claim: The first sight on earth left only a remote possibility that the figure was a jinn, despite Muhammad’s necessary knowledge that he was an angel; seeing him at the Sidra above the sixth heaven excludes jinn or human presence.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.anchor: فلما رآه عند سدرة المنتهى وهو فوق السماء السادسة لم يحتمل أن يكون هناك جن ولا إنس

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r2.claim: Rāzī allows the wāw in the question to coordinate or introduce a circumstantial clause: how can they dispute what he saw when he saw it without doubt?
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r2.anchor: المسألة الأولى : الواو يحتمل أن تكون عاطفة

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r5.claim: Nazlatan is a verbal noun on the faʿla pattern from descending, so an agent must have descended; the identity of the pronoun in “he saw him” determines the options.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r5.anchor: فعلة من النزول فهي كجلسة من الجلوس

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r6.claim: If the pronoun refers to God, following the interpretation of “what he saw” in 53:11, Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart twice.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r6.anchor: في قوله { ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى }

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r7.claim: One proposed sense is God’s physical movement or relocation; Rāzī rejects this as false.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r7.anchor: قول من يجوز على الله تعالى الحركة والانتقال وهو باطل

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r8.claim: The other proposed sense is nonphysical nearness: God draws his servant near through mercy and favor, without the servant seeing him.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r8.anchor: فإن الله تعالى قد يقرب بالرحمة والفضل من عبده ولا يراه العبد

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r1.claim: For the view that Muhammad saw God, Rāzī offers the image of the Prophet descending on the mount of passion and the vehicle of the self.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نزل على متن الهوى ومركب النفس

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r2.claim: Alternatively, “descent” can stand for ascent’s opposite, marking the event as the worldly ascent, which has a return, unlike the ascent of the hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r2.anchor: أن المراد من النزلة ضدها وهي العرجة كأنه قال رآه عرجة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r3.claim: A second major view takes the pronoun as Gabriel: Muhammad saw Gabriel during another descent.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r3.anchor: أنه عائد إلى جبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r4.claim: Rāzī cites an account of the Night Journey: Muhammad passed beyond Gabriel, who said that advancing a finger further would burn him, then returned to Gabriel; this is one explanation of the descent.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r4.anchor: وقال له جبريل عليه السلام لو دنوت أنملة لاحترقت

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r5.claim: The return may be called “another” because Muhammad repeatedly passed Gabriel and descended back to him during the repeated trips concerning prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r5.anchor: لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في أمر الصلاة تردد مرارا فربما كان يجاوز كل مرة

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r6.claim: Alternatively, the descent belongs to Gabriel, who descended to Muhammad twice while appearing in his own form.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون لجبريل عليه السلام وكلاهما منقول وعلى هذا الوجه فنزلة أخرى ظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.claim: If the pronoun means God, reading “at the Sidra” as God’s location in a place is false; it can instead describe Muhammad as the one who was at the Sidra when he saw.
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.anchor: قول من يجعل الله في مكان وهو باطل

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.claim: If the referent is Gabriel, either account of “at the Sidra” works, but Rāzī says Muhammad being there with Gabriel is clearer.
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.anchor: وكون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع جبريل عند سدرة المنتهى أظهر

STUDYQURAN:53:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r1.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r1.claim: The verse may refer either to the Prophet seeing Gabriel in his true form twice or to two distinct visions of God.
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r1.anchor: This verse refers to either the two times in which the Prophet is said to have seen Gabriel in his true form or two separate visions of God (Aj).

STUDYQURAN:53:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r2.claim: The Prophet is said to have seen Gabriel's true form twice: at Mount Ḥirāʾ during the first revelation and again during the Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r2.anchor: The Prophet is said to have seen Gabriel’s true form only twice, once at Mount Ḥirāʾ, where he received the first revelation, and a second time during the Ascension.

STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.speaker: those who maintain the vision of God
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.claim: Proponents of the God-vision interpretation say the Prophet saw his Lord twice in special Self-Disclosure: above the Throne at the highest veil and at the Lote Tree of the Boundary.
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.anchor: Those who maintain that it refers to the vision of God say that the Prophet saw his Lord twice in a special Self-Disclosure

TAB-FULL:v22p29/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p29/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p29/r1.claim: The verse says that Muhammad saw him another time; exegetes disagree over whom he saw, as they did about 53:11.
TAB-FULL:v22p29/r1.anchor: عن عائشة، أن عائشة قالت: يا أبا عائشة من زعم أن محمدا، رأى ربه فقد أعظم الفرية على الله

TAB-FULL:v22p29/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p29/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v22p29/r2.claim: Aisha rejects the claim that Muhammad saw God and identifies the one seen twice as Gabriel in his created form, once in the heavens and once descending and filling the space between heaven and earth; she says the Prophet confirmed this. She invokes 81:23, 6:103, and 42:51.
TAB-FULL:v22p29/r2.anchor: عن عائشة، أن عائشة قالت: يا أبا عائشة من زعم أن محمدا، رأى ربه فقد أعظم الفرية على الله

TAB-FULL:v22p32/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud says Muhammad saw Gabriel in a celestial rafraf that filled the space between heaven and earth.
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} [النجم: 13] قال: «رأى جبريل في رفرف قد ملأ ما بين السماء والأرض»

TAB-FULL:v22p32/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r2.claim: In another report Ibn Masʿud describes Gabriel's legs as having pearls like drops on greenery.
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r2.anchor: عن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} [النجم: 13] قال: «رأى جبريل في وبر رجليه كالدر، مثل القطر على البقل»

TAB-FULL:v22p32/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r3.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet saw Gabriel in his own form twice.
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} [النجم: 13] قال: «رأى جبريل في صورته مرتين»

TAB-FULL:v22p32/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ identifies the one seen on the second occasion as Gabriel.
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r4.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، عن الربيع، {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} [النجم: 13] قال: «جبريل عليه السلام»

TAB-FULL:v22p32/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r5.speaker: كعب
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r5.claim: Kaʿb says God divided vision and speech between Moses and Muhammad: He spoke with Moses twice and Muhammad saw Him twice.
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r5.anchor: عن كعب، أنه أخبره «أن الله تبارك وتعالى قسم رؤيته وكلامه بين موسى ومحمد، فكلمه موسى مرتين، ورآه محمد مرتين»

TAB-FULL:v22p32/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r6.claim: Aisha says whoever claims Muhammad saw God, knew the unseen future, or concealed revelation lies; she cites 6:103, 42:51, 31:34, and 5:67, and says Muhammad instead saw Gabriel twice in his form.
TAB-FULL:v22p32/r6.anchor: فقالت: سبحان الله لقد قف شعري لما قلت: أين أنت من ثلاثة من حدثك بهن فقد كذب، من أخبرك أن محمدا رأى ربه فقد كذب

TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Messenger saw his Lord with his heart.
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قال: {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} [النجم: 13] قال: «إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى ربه بقلبه»

TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r2.claim: Answering an objection about 6:103, Ikrima compares divine sight to seeing the sky: seeing it does not mean seeing all of it.
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r2.anchor: قال له عكرمة: أليس ترى السماء؟ قال: بلى، أفكلها ترى؟

TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r3.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the Lord drew near and revealed to His servant, and Ibn Abbas concludes that the Prophet saw Him.
TAB-FULL:v22p32#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله: {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى} [النجم: 14] قال: «دنا ربه فتدلى، فكان قاب قوسين أو أدنى، فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى»

BURSEVI:v9p184/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p184/r2.claim: The pronoun in raʾāhu refers to Gabriel; the Prophet saw him in his true form once more during one of the descents on the Night Journey.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r2.anchor: الضمير البارز في رآه لجبريل ونزلة منصوب نصب الظرف الذي هو مرة

BURSEVI:v9p184/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p184/r3.claim: Nazlatan is an adverbial accusative meaning one more time, since the noun denotes a single occurrence of an action.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r3.anchor: لأن الفعلة اسم للمرة من الفعل فكانت في حكمها والمعنى وبالله لقد رأى محمد جبريل

BURSEVI:v9p184/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p184/r4.claim: The Prophet made repeated ascents to seek a reduction in the prescribed prayers; Gabriel remained behind at the Sidrah, saying that an inch farther would burn him, and the Prophet saw him there with six hundred wings shedding pearls and rubies.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r4.anchor: وذلك أنه كان للنبي عليه السلام في ليلة المعراج عرجات لمسألة التخفيف من إعداد الصلوات المفروضة

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r3.claim: Nazla is a noun of occurrence meaning one descent; the verse describes a sighting during a different descent from the preceding one.
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r3.anchor: النزلة بناء مرة من النزول فمعناه نزول واحد

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r4.claim: The reported reading takes the subject as the Prophet and the object as Gabriel; the second descent is Gabriel's descent to take him to heaven.
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r4.anchor: ضمير الفاعل المستكن في قوله { رآه } للنبي

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r6.claim: Al-Tabatabai instead takes the object pronoun as God and the vision as heart-sight: during his ascent the Prophet descended at the Lote Tree and saw God with his heart, as at the first descent.
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r6.anchor: صحة إرجاع ضمير المفعول إليه تعالى والمراد بالرؤية رؤية القلب

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi places the second vision at Sidra in the seventh heaven.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.anchor: في قوله تعالى { ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى } قال في السماء السابعة

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.claim: Al-Tabatabai directs readers to his earlier account of the Mi‘raj reports in the opening commentary on Surat al-Isra, where he reviewed their differing descriptions.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم في أول تفسير سورة الإسراء روايات جامعة لقصة معراجه

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.claim: The earlier discussion recorded disagreement over whether the Mi‘raj occurred in a dream or while awake, and whether an awake ascent involved body and soul or the soul alone.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.anchor: الاختلاف في كيفية معراجه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه كان في المنام أو في اليقظة

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r10.speaker: صاحب المناقب
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r10.claim: The Sahib al-Manaqib says the Imamis hold that the journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque occurred in body and soul, as the Isra verse indicates.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r10.anchor: عن صاحب المناقب أن الإمامية ترى أن إسراءه من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى كان بالروح والجسم معا

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r11.speaker: قوم وكثير من الشيعة
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r11.claim: Some say the ascent from Jerusalem to the heavens was in both body and soul; many Shi‘a agree with this view.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r11.anchor: وأما من المسجد الأقصى إلى السماوات فقد قال قوم بكونه بالروح والجسم معا أيضا ووافقهم كثير من الشيعة

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r12.speaker: بعض الشيعة وبعض المتأخرين
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r12.claim: Some incline to a soul-only ascent from Jerusalem to heaven, and some later scholars also lean toward that position.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r12.anchor: ومال بعضهم إلى كونه بالروح ومال إليه بعض المتأخرين

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r14.claim: The interpretation that the Isra occurred in a dream is not one to be considered.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r14.anchor: وأما كون الإسراء في المنام فقد تقدم في تفسير آية الإسراء أنه مما لا ينبغي أن يلتفت إليه

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.claim: Explaining the ascent as night travel to other planets, star systems, or galaxies conflicts with the detailed reports and has no coherent fit with the verses.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.anchor: فمما لا يلائمه الأخبار الواردة في تفصيل القصة البتة بل ولا محصل مضامين الآيات المتقدمة

TABRISI:53:12-13/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:12-13/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:12-13/r6.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel in his created form descending from heaven a second time, having seen him twice in that form.
TABRISI:53:12-13/r6.anchor: رأى جبرائيل في صورته التي خلق عليها نازلا من السماء نزلة أخرى

THALABI:v9p142/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p142/r1.speaker: عائشة وأكثر العلماء
THALABI:v9p142/r1.claim: The author prefers Aisha’s and most scholars’ view that Muhammad saw Gabriel in his created form twice, first at the highest horizon and again at the Sidra; the location and ‘another time’ favor this, since God is not located or subject to descent and there was no prior vision of God before the Night Journey.
THALABI:v9p142/r1.anchor: وهذا قول عائشة وأكثر العلماء وهو الاختيار، لأنه قرن الرؤية بالمكان فقال عند سدرة المنتهى

THALABI:v9p142/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p142/r2.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v9p142/r2.claim: Aisha calls it a grave slander to claim Muhammad saw his Lord; she says he saw Gabriel twice in his original form, once filling the span between heaven and earth and once at the Sidra, and the Prophet said ‘It is Gabriel.’
THALABI:v9p142/r2.anchor: قالت: إنما هو جبريل رآه على صورته التي خلق عليها مرتين: مرة حين هبط من السماء إلى الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r1.speaker: أكثر العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r1.claim: Most scholars say Muhammad saw Gabriel in his form twice, as discussed earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r1.anchor: أكثر العلماء على أن اههنى أشبه رأى جبريل في صورته مرتين على ما ذكرنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad saw his Lord, following his interpretation of 53:11.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رأى ربه على ما ذكرنا في قوله: {ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r3.claim: On Ibn Abbas's reading, نزلة أخرى refers to Muhammad: it is reported that he repeatedly ascended while asking God to reduce the required prayers, so he may have seen God on one descent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r3.anchor: وقد روي أنه كانت له عرجات في تلك الليلة لما استحط ربه من أعداد الصلوات المفروضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p29#2/r4.claim: The pronoun هو refers to Muhammad.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r5.claim: The author identifies the one seen as Muhammad's Lord.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r5.anchor: ولقد رآه } ربه. وقيل: رأى جبريل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r6.claim: An alternative view says Muhammad saw Gabriel in the form in which he was created.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r6.anchor: وقيل: رأى جبريل على صورته التي خلق عليها

QASHANI:53:13-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:13-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:13-15/r1.claim: On the return from the Real and descent to the spirit's station, the Prophet saw Gabriel in his true form again.
QASHANI:53:13-15/r1.anchor: عند الرجوع عن الحق والنزول إلى مقام الروح

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r3.claim: The present tense in “he sees” indicates continuing vision, and the following oath explicitly confirms that the Prophet saw him again.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r3.anchor: Muzâri‘sîgasıyla يَرَىٰ buyurulması rü’yetin istimrârına delâlet eder.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r4.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel, the strong one and possessor of mirra, again in his true form during the descent from the Mi'raj; this indicates Gabriel's rank was below the Prophet's.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r4.anchor: Bir de o gördüğü Şedîdü’l-kuvâ Zû-mirre’yi, yani hakīkī sureti ve bütün kuvâsı ve kuvveti ile kendini tâlim eden Cibrîl’i bir de Mi‘râc’dan inerken gördü.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r5.speaker: müfessirînin çoğu
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r5.claim: Most commentators parse nazlatan, as a once-form verbal noun, as an adverb meaning “on another occasion, in a descent.”
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r5.anchor: Müfessirînin çoğu diyorlar ki: نَزْلَةً masdar binâ-i merre

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r6.speaker: Hûfî ve İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r6.claim: Hufi and Ibn Atiyya instead treat nazlatan as a verbal noun in circumstantial position, meaning “while descending.”
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r6.anchor: ve İbn Atıyye gibi bazıları da hâl mevkiinde masdar olduğunu söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r7.claim: On the adverbial reading, ukhra qualifies nazla as another descent; on the circumstantial reading it means another time, or modifies ra'a as another vision.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r7.anchor: أُخْرَىٰ evvelkine göre نَزْلَةً’in sıfatı, “diğer bir iniş”, ikinciye göre de مَ َّرةً أُخْرَى

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r8.claim: Commentators agree this descent took place on the Mi'raj night but differ over whose descent it was.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r8.anchor: Bu inişin Mi‘râc gecesi olduğunda ittifak vardır.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r9.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r9.claim: Razi rejects physical motion or descent for God; spiritual descent means approaching the servant with mercy and favor. He reads Moses' request as asking God to remove veils of majesty and approach graciously so he may see.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r9.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Allah teâlâ hakkında hareket ve nüzul tasavvuru bâtıldır. Manevî kurb ile nüzul ise rahmet ve fazl ile abdine yaklaşır da abd onu görmez.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r10.speaker: birçokları
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r10.claim: Many identify the descending figure as Gabriel in his true form.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r10.anchor: Birçokları Cibrîl’in hakīkī sureti ile nüzûlü demişlerdir.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.claim: Elmalili rejects Gabriel as the descending figure because Gabriel cannot pass the Sidra, so the location beside it does not fit a descent by him from above.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.anchor: Lâkin Cibrîl Sidre-i Müntehâ’dan öte geçemediğine göre

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r12.claim: Elmalili takes it as the Prophet's descent from the Mi'raj, following the report that Gabriel stopped short because he would burn if he came a fingertip closer, while the Prophet passed beyond and Gabriel later returned to meet him.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r12.anchor: Râzî ve Nîsâbûrî’nin kaydettikleri vechile Mi‘râc haberlerinde vârid olduğuna göre Mi‘râc gecesi Cibrîl

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r13.claim: The Prophet went up and down several times when prayer was prescribed, so “another descent” aptly denotes the final descent; he saw Gabriel in assumed form at Qur'anic revelations and in true form once before and once during the Mi'raj return.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r13.anchor: Resûlullah namaz emrinde birkaç kereler inip çıkmış idi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.claim: The mysterious, vivid scene points to faith about what senses cannot reach and warns against straining reason beyond its limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.anchor: duyularla algılanamayan, fizik âlemin ötesine taşan konularda imanın esas olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.claim: The passage condemns pagan attempts to make divinity concrete through material or spiritual intermediaries and to ascribe godhood to beings besides God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.anchor: Allah’tan başka varlıklara tanrılık izâfe etme telakkisini mahkûm etme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.claim: Although the sūra is early Meccan, these verses, especially 13–18, are generally understood as relating to the Miʿrāj near the end of the Meccan period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.anchor: 13-18. âyetlerin, Mekke döneminin sonlarına doğru gerçekleştiği bilinen mi‘rac olayı ile ilgili olduğu kabul edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.claim: If the scene is the Miʿrāj, appearance, horizon, Sidra, descent, and nearness are figurative descriptions of divine acts and attributes, understood without asking how or how much.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.anchor: “görünme, yüce ufukta, sidretü’l-müntehâda olma, inme, çok yaklaşma” gibi ifadeleri mecazi mânada almak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r38.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r38.claim: The commentary offers both “saw him once more during another descent beside the Sidra” and its own rendering, “saw him during descent beside the Sidra.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r38.anchor: “Andolsun ki onu bir başka iniş esnasında da sidretü’l-müntehânın yanında bir daha gördü” veya

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r39.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r39.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r39.claim: Those preferring “another descent” see an indication that the Prophet’s rank surpassed Gabriel’s.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r39.anchor: Birinci mânayı tercih edenlere göre burada, Resûlullah’ın mertebesinin Cebrâil’den üstün olduğuna işaret bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r40.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r40.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r40.claim: Some take “descent” as Gabriel’s descent; a reading that makes it God’s descent is mentioned but judged weak.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r40.anchor: Bu kelimenin Allah Teâlâ hakkında olduğu yorumu da yapılmış olmakla beraber bu zayıf bulunmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.claim: Elmalılı’s summary says Gabriel appeared in whatever form he took during each Qur’anic revelation, but in his true form only once before the Miʿrāj and once while descending from it, meeting the Prophet at the Sidra.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.anchor: Resûlullah, Cebrâil’i Kur’an’ın her inen parçası esnasında, hangi sûrete girmişse öyle görüyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r58.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r58.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r58.claim: Elmalılı finds “a final descent” the more meaningful rendering because Muhammad made several ascents and descents during the Miʿrāj for prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r58.anchor: 13. âyetteki “nezleten uhrâ” tamlamasını “son bir iniş” şeklinde düşünmek daha mânidar olur

BURHAN:v4p290/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p290/r4.claim: ʿInd and ladā can denote literal nearness, as in the Prophet’s sighting at the Lote Tree and Joseph’s master at the door.

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r16.claim: The author says Gabriel saw God once again while Muhammad was at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r16.anchor: أي جبريل رأى الله مرة أخرى حين كان محمد عند سدرة المنتهى

TUSTARI:53:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:13/r1.claim: Sahl says the vision occurred at the beginning, when God created him.
TUSTARI:53:13/r1.anchor: يعني في الابتداء حين خلقه الله سبحانه وتعالى

TUSTARI:53:13/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:13/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:13/r2.claim: Another account describes him as a light in a column of light a million years before creation, with faith's innate qualities, unveiling the unseen through the unseen and worshipping before God.
TUSTARI:53:13/r2.anchor: ويقال نورا في عامود النور قبل بدء الخلق بألف ألف عام بطبائع الإيمان

NAHHAS:v4p268/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p268/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p268/r5.claim: The soundest interpretation is that the pronoun refers to Gabriel, described earlier as mighty in strength.
NAHHAS:v4p268/r5.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه وأصحه أن الضمير يعود على شديد القوى

NAHHAS:v4p268/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p268/r6.speaker: عائشة
NAHHAS:v4p268/r6.claim: ʿAʾisha says Muhammad saw Gabriel descending and filling the horizon with his form and majesty; she cites this against the claim that Muhammad saw God.
NAHHAS:v4p268/r6.anchor: قالت أنا سألت عن ذلك نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال رأيت جبرائيل صلى الله عليه وسلم نزل سادا الأفق على خلقه وهيبته

NAHHAS:v4p268/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p268/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p268/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ glosses nazlatan ukhrā as another time.
NAHHAS:v4p268/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء نزلة أخرى مرة أخرى

NAHHAS:v4p268/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p268/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p268/r8.claim: Al-Nahhas parses nazlatan as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially, meaning that Gabriel was seen while descending again.
NAHHAS:v4p268/r8.anchor: نزلة مصدر في موضع الحال كما تقول جاء فلان مشيا أي ماشيا والتقدير ولقد رآه نازلا نزلة أخرى

SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses نزلة as an adverb meaning once, since a noun of one occurrence functions as an adverb; al-Samin says this is al-Farra's school, not the Basrans'.
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " نصب الظرف الذي هو مرة؛ لأن الفعلة اسم للمرة من الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r2.claim: Makki, al-Hawfi, and Ibn ʿAtiyya parse نزلة as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially: he saw him descending another time.
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r2.anchor: قال مكي: " أي: رآه نازلا نزلة أخرى " ، وإليه ذهب الحوفي وابن عطية.

SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses نزلة as an emphatic verbal noun, expanded as مرة أخرى or رؤية أخرى; the author questions construing it as رؤية.
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r3.anchor: فقدره أبو البقاء: " مرة أخرى أو رؤية أخرى ". قلت: وفي تأويل " نزلة " برؤية نظر.

SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r4.claim: أخرى indicates that a previous vision had occurred.
SAMIN-DURR:53:13/r4.anchor: و " أخرى " تدل على سبق رؤية قبلها.

ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n9/r1.claim: The one seen a second time was the angel manifested in his true shape and nature.
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n9/r1.anchor: he saw the angel "manifested in his true shape and nature".

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r1.claim: Mirya is doubt or casting suspicion, unlike argument over ideas: the disbelievers challenged the report, not the vision itself, so the verse says not to dispute what he sees.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r1.anchor: فالكفار كانوا يشككون في الرواية وليس في الأفكار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r3.claim: Nazla, from descending, is more specific than marra: Muhammad saw Gabriel on his descent back, after ascending above the place Gabriel could reach.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r3.anchor: استخدم كلمة نزلة وليس كلمة (مرة) لأن النزلة من النزول فقال ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r4.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r4.claim: The author cites Gabriel telling the Prophet to proceed and saying that he would have been burned had he advanced farther, as support for the Prophet's greater ascent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r4.anchor: أن جبريل - عليه السلام - قال للرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - تقدم وقال لو تقدمتُ لاحترقت

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r1.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel again in the form in which God created him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r1.anchor: أي رأى النبي جبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم في صورته التي خلقه الله تعالى عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r2.claim: Nazlatan means another descent, a single instance used adverbially; unlike marra, it implies descent and approach.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r2.anchor: أي مرة أخرى من النزول وهي فعلة من النزول أقيمت مقام المرة ونصبت نصبها على الظرفية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r3.speaker: الحوفي وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r3.claim: Al-Hawfi and Ibn Atiyya parse nazlatan as a verbal noun functioning as an anticipated circumstantial phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r3.anchor: وقال الحوفي وابن عطية : إن نزلة منصوب على المصدرية للحال المقدرة أي نازلا نزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows nazlatan as a cognate accusative meaning another vision; Alusi finds it problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r4.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء كونه منصوبا على المصدرية لرأى من معناه أي رؤية أخرى وفيه نظر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r5.claim: The statement removes doubt about the later vision, which took place on the Night Journey.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50/r5.anchor: نفي الريبة والشك عن المرة الأخيرة وكانت ليلة الإسراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وعائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r4.claim: Ibn Masud and Aisha are among those who say the vision was of Gabriel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r4.anchor: فقال قوم: رأى جبريل، وهو قول ابن مسعود وعائشة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r6.claim: Another group says the one seen was God, then differs over whether the vision was with the heart or the eye.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو الله عز وجل. ثم اختلفوا في معنى الرؤية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad saw God with his heart twice, linking this verse with the later vision at another descent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: جعل بصره في فؤاده فرآه بفؤاده، وهو قول ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explicitly reports that Muhammad saw God twice with his heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس: "ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى". "ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى" قال: رآه بفؤاده مرتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r9.speaker: أنس والحسن وعكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r9.claim: Anas, al-Hasan, and Ikrima are among those who say Muhammad saw his Lord with his eyes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r9.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أنه رآه بعينه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r10.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r10.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas's saying that God chose Abraham for intimate friendship, Moses for speech, and Muhammad for vision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r10.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: إن الله اصطفى إبراهيم بالخلة واصطفى موسى بالكلام واصطفى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بالرؤية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r11.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r11.claim: Aisha holds the Prophet did not see his Lord and understands the vision as Gabriel in his form twice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r11.anchor: وكانت عائشة رضي الله عنها تقول: لم ير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه، وتحمل الآية على رؤيته جبريل عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r12.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r12.claim: Aisha says anyone who claims Muhammad saw God lies, citing verses that deny vision, describe God's speech, deny knowledge of tomorrow, and command the Messenger to convey revelation; she says he saw Gabriel twice in his form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p403/r12.anchor: من حدثك أن محمدا رأى ربه فقد كذب، ثم قرأت: "لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#2/r4.claim: Muhammad saw Gabriel in his created form descending from heaven on another occasion; he saw that form twice, once on earth and once in heaven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#2/r4.anchor: رأى جبريل في صورته التي خلق عليها نازلا من السماء نزلة أخرى، وذلك أنه رآه في صورته مرتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the other descent through the Prophet's repeated ascents to request fewer prayers; on a descent he saw his Lord, and Ibn Abbas also reports a heart-vision and an eye-vision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r1.anchor: وعلى قول ابن عباس معنى: "نزلة أخرى" هو أنه كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عرجات في تلك الليلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r4.claim: Nazlatan is a noun of one occurrence in the accusative as an adverbial; it indicates this vision too accompanied descent and nearness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r4.anchor: مرة أخرى فعلة من النزول أقيمت مقام المرة ونصبت نصبها

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r5.claim: Alternatively, he saw Gabriel descending another descent; the accusative is a verbal noun, and the point is to remove doubt about the later vision.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r5.anchor: وقيل تقديره ولقد رآه نازلا نزلة أخرى

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r6.claim: The identity of the one seen and the account of the approach are as already explained above.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r6.anchor: والكلام في المرئي والدنو ما سبق

BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r4.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r4.claim: When Masruq cited the two verses against her denial that the Prophet saw God, Aisha said he had seen Gabriel, not in his created form except twice, descending and filling the space between heaven and earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r4.anchor: عن مسروق أنه قال لعائشة رضي الله عنها لما أنكرت الرؤية : ألم يقل الله تعالى { ولقد رآه بالأفق المين }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas said, in a report in Muslim, that the Prophet saw Him with his heart twice.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r6.anchor: ثم روي من صحيح مسلم عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : ) رآه بفؤاده مرتين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r8.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r8.claim: Ibn Barjan treats sleep, swooning, and death as signs preceding encounter with God; the Night Journey left ordinary worldly perception for the higher, unseen realm, so sight there should not be denied.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p318/r8.anchor: وقال ابن برجان ما معناه : إن النوم والصعق من آيات الله على لقاء الله وهي مقدمات لذلك , ولكل حقيقة حق يتقدمها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r3.claim: The pronoun in “he saw him” may refer to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r3.anchor: قال مؤكدا لأجل إنكارهم : { ولقد رآه } أي الله تعالى أو جبرئيل عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r4.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to Gabriel in his true form.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r4.anchor: قال مؤكدا لأجل إنكارهم : { ولقد رآه } أي الله تعالى أو جبرئيل عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r5.claim: A report in Muslim from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet saw Him with his heart twice.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r5.anchor: روى مسلم في الإيمان عن عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال { ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى } { ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى } , قال : ( رآه بفؤاده مرتين )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r6.speaker: ابن مرجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r6.claim: Ibn Marjan divided the Night Journey into two: an initial sight by the heart as preparation, then this second sight by the eye.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r6.anchor: قال : ( رآه بفؤاده مرتين ) وجعل ابن مرجان الإسراء مرتين : الأولى بالفؤاد مقدمة وهذه بالعين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r7.claim: “Nazlatan” is accusative as an adverbial of time because the form means one descent or occurrence; the next phrase specifies the place.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r7.anchor: عبر بقوله : { نزلة } وانتصب على الظرفية لأن الفعلة بمعنى المرة الأعلى , وعين الوقت بتعين المكان فقال :

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.claim: He places the second descent at the Night Journey, shortly before the Hijra in the thirteenth year of prophethood, after ascent through the stations, where the pen-scratching was heard.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.anchor: وذلك - والله أعلم - ليلة الإسراء في السنة الثالثة عشرة من النبوة قبل الهجرة بقليل بعد الترقي في معراج الكمالات

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad saw his Lord twice with his heart.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى أفتمارونه على ما يرى ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} قال: رأى محمد ربه بقلبه مرتين

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r1.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r1.claim: Anas reports that Muhammad saw his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r1.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: رأى محمد ربه

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet saw his Lord with his eyes.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى ربه بعينه

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad saw his Lord twice, once with his eyesight and once with his heart.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن محمدا رأى ربه مرتين مرة ببصره ومرة بفؤاده

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas affirms that the Prophet saw his Lord; al-Tirmidhi grades this report good.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله الله {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} قال ابن عباس: قد رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه عز وجل

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r5.speaker: كعب وابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r5.claim: Kaʿb confirms Ibn Abbas's claim that Muhammad saw his Lord twice, contrasting Muhammad's vision with Moses's speech to God twice.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: إنا بنو هاشم نزعم أن نقول: إن محمدا قد رأى ربه مرتين فقال كعب: إن الله قسم رؤيته وكلامه بين موسى ومحمد

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r6.claim: Aisha rejects the claim that Muhammad saw God, calling it a grave falsehood; she says he saw Gabriel, not his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r6.anchor: قالت: أين يذهب بك إنما هو جبريل من أخبرك أن محمدا رأى ربه

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r7.claim: Aisha says the Prophet saw Gabriel in his true form only twice, at the Sidrah and at Ajyad, with six hundred wings filling the horizon.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r7.anchor: ولكنه رأى جبريل لم يره في صورته إلا مرتين مرة عند سدرة المنتهى ومرة عند أجياد له ستمائة جناح قد سد الأفق

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas asks whether it is surprising that intimacy belongs to Abraham, speech to Moses, and vision to Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أتعجبون أن تكون الخلة لإبراهيم والكلام لموسى والرؤية لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r9.claim: Ikrima says Muhammad saw his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: رأى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه

DURR-FULL:v7p647/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet saw his Lord in the most beautiful form, who placed a hand between his shoulders; its coolness reached his chest and he learned what was in heaven and earth.
DURR-FULL:v7p647/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: رأيت ربي في أحسن صورة فقال لي: يا محمد هل تدري فيم يختصم الملأ الأعلى

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr neither asserts nor denies that the Prophet saw God.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: ما أزعم أنه رآه وما أزعم أنه لم يره

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r2.claim: Asked whether he saw his Lord, the Prophet replied that there was light and asked how he could see Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل رأيت ربك فقال: نور أنى أراه

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r3.claim: A second report from Abu Dharr has the Prophet answer that he saw a light.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي ذر أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل رأيت ربك فقال: رأيت نورا

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r4.claim: Abu Dharr says the Prophet saw his Lord with his heart, not his eyes.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: رآه بقلبه ولم يره بعينيه

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r5.claim: Another report from Abu Dharr specifies that the Prophet saw his Lord with his heart, not his eyesight.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه بقلبه ولم يره ببصره

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra identifies the one the Prophet saw as Gabriel.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة في قوله {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} قال: رأى جبريل عليه السلام

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r7.claim: Ibrahim says the Prophet saw Gabriel in his own form.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: رأى جبريل في صورته

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r8.speaker: مرة الهمداني
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r8.claim: Murra al-Hamdani says Gabriel came in his true form only twice and was seen adorned in green with pearls hanging from him.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r8.anchor: عن مرة الهمداني قال: لم يأته جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين فرآه في خضر يتعلق به الدر

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r9.claim: Qatada says the Prophet saw a great light at the Sidrah of the Utmost Boundary.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} قال: رأى نورا عظيما عند سدرة المنتهى

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r10.claim: Ibn Masud says Gabriel was seen hanging a leg at the Sidrah, with pearls like raindrops on plants.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} قال: رأى جبريل معلقا رجله بسدرة عليه الدر كأنه قطر المطر على البقل

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r11.claim: Ibn Masud describes Gabriel at the Sidrah in his true form with six hundred wings, one filling the horizon, shedding wondrous jewels.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى} قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل في صورته عند السدرة له ستمائة جناح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.claim: The account advances from denied earthly sight to a greater sight in the upper realm, moving upward through the manifestations of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.anchor: أي إن كنتم تجحدون رؤيته جبريل في الأرض فلقد رآه رؤية أعظم منها إذ رآه في العالم العلوي مصاحبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r8.claim: The oath lām and qad stress the unusual sight, ascent to heaven, and Muhammad's great rank.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r8.anchor: فتأكيد الكلام بلام القسم وحرف التحقيق لأجل ما في هذا الخبر من الغرابة من حيث هو قد رأى جبريل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r9.claim: The subject pronoun in raʾāhu refers to ‘your companion’ in 53:2; its object refers to Gabriel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r9.anchor: فضمير الرفع في { رءاه } عائد إلى { صاحبكم } ( النجم : 2 ) ، وضمير النصب عائد إلى جبريل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r10.claim: Nazla is a verbal noun indicating one descent; ukhrā relates it to ‘he drew near and descended’ in 53:8.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r10.anchor: و { نزلة } فعلة من النزول فهو مصدر دال على المرة : أي في مكان آخر من النزول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r1.claim: Nazlatan can be parsed with an elided preposition, as a locative adverb, or with an omitted noun meaning ‘at the time of another descent,’ as a temporal adverb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r1.anchor: وانتصاب { نزلة } على نزع الخافض ، أو على النيابة عن ظرف المكان ، أو على حذف مضاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب الأحبار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r7.claim: They take the pronoun in رآه to refer to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وكعب الأحبار: هو عائد على الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وعائشة ومجاهد والربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r8.claim: They take the pronoun in رآه to refer to Gabriel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r8.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وعائشة ومجاهد والربيع: هو عائد على جبريل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r9.claim: نزلة means one time or occurrence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r9.anchor: و: نزلة معناه: مرة، ونصبه على المصدر في موضع الحال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r10.claim: نزلة is accusative as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r10.anchor: ونصبه على المصدر في موضع الحال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains nazlatan ukhrā as ‘another time.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج أي رآه مرة أخرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muhammad saw his Lord again; during repeated ascents for the prayers he saw Him on one of those occasions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رأى محمد ربه وبيان هذا أنه تردد لأجل الصلوات مرارا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r3.speaker: كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r3.claim: Kaʿb says God apportioned speech and vision between Muhammad and Moses: Muhammad saw God twice and Moses spoke with Him twice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r3.anchor: قال كعب إن الله تعالى قسم كلامه ورؤيته بين محمد وموسى فرآه محمد مرتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd identifies the one seen as Gabriel, whom Muhammad saw in the form in which he was created.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن مسعود أن هذه الرؤية لجبريل أيضا رآه على صورته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report in Muslim, says Muhammad saw Him with his heart twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r3.speaker: أبو صالح، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r3.claim: Abu Salih, al-Suddi, and others likewise say the vision was with the heart, reported as twice or once.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r3.anchor: وكذا قال أبو صالح والسدي وغيرهما: إنه رآه بفؤاده مرتين [أو مرة]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r4.claim: Ibn Masud and others differed; one report from him states the vision without specifying the heart, which Ibn Kathir construes as the restricted heart vision.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says reports that Muhammad saw God with physical eyesight are anomalous and that no sound Companion report establishes this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r5.anchor: ومن روى عنه بالبصر فقد أغرب، فإنه لا يصح في ذلك شيء عن الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r6.speaker: البغوي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi reports that a group, including Anas, al-Hasan, and Ikrima, held that Muhammad saw God with his eye.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r6.anchor: وقول البغوي في تفسيره: وذهب جماعة إلى أنه رآه بعينه، وهو قول أنس والحسن وعكرمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir questions al-Baghawi's attribution of physical sight to Anas, al-Hasan, and Ikrima.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r7.anchor: وهو قول أنس والحسن وعكرمة. فيه نظر، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r8.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports Ibn Abbas saying Muhammad saw his Lord twice, explaining that God's eyes are not perceived when He manifests in His own light; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: رأى محمد ربه. قلت: أليس الله يقول: {لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r9.speaker: كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r9.claim: Al-Sha'bi recounts Ka'b's view that God divided vision and speech between Muhammad and Moses: Moses spoke with God twice, while Muhammad saw Him twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r9.anchor: فقال كعب: إن الله قسم رؤيته وكلامه بين محمد وموسى، فكلم موسى مرتين ورآه محمد مرتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r10.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r10.claim: Aisha tells Masruq that Muhammad saw Gabriel, not God, twice in Gabriel's original form, at Sidrat al-Muntaha and Ajyad; she calls claims of divine sight or concealed revelation a grave lie and cites the verse about the greatest signs and 31:34.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r10.anchor: وقال مسروق: دخلت على عائشة فقلت: هل رأى محمد ربه؟ فقالت: لقد تكلمت بشيء قف له شعري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.claim: This is the second time Muhammad saw Gabriel in his created form, on the Night Journey; Ibn Kathir says earlier Isra reports already supply the details.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.anchor: هذه هي المرة الثانية التي رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها جبريل على صورته التي خلقه الله عليها، وكانت ليلة الإسراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas affirms a vision on the Night Journey and cites this verse as evidence; a group of early and later authorities follows him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r4.anchor: وتقدم أن ابن عباس، رضي الله عنهما، كان يثبت الرؤية ليلة الإسراء، ويستشهد بهذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r5.speaker: جماعات من الصحابة والتابعين وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r5.claim: Other groups of Companions, Successors, and later authorities disagreed with Ibn Abbas's affirmation of the vision on the Night Journey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r5.anchor: وقد خالفه جماعات من الصحابة، رضي الله عنهم، والتابعين وغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet saw Gabriel with six hundred wings, from which pearl, ruby, and other marvels fell; Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and strong.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r7.claim: A second report says Gabriel in his own form had six hundred wings, each spanning the horizon and shedding pearls and rubies; Ibn Kathir grades its chain hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل في صورته وله ستمائة جناح، كل جناح منها قد سد الأفق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r3.claim: Aisha rejects claims that Muhammad saw God, knew the unseen, or concealed revelation; she cites 6:103, 42:51, 31:34, and 5:67, and says he saw Gabriel in his original form twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r3.anchor: أتى مسروق عائشة فقال: يا أم المؤمنين، هل رأى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه عز وجل؟ قالت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r4.claim: In another report, Aisha says she was the first to ask Muhammad about these verses; he answered that they refer to Gabriel, whom he saw in his created form only twice, once descending and filling the space between heaven and earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي، عن مسروق قال: كنت عند عائشة فقلت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r1.claim: Abu Dharr says he asked the Prophet whether he had seen his Lord; the answer is phrased as seeing light, with Muslim transmitting variant wordings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هل رأيت ربك؟ فقال: "نور أنى أراه".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r2.speaker: أحمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r2.claim: Al-Khallal reports that Ahmad remained opposed to this hadith and did not know how to understand it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r2.anchor: وقد حكى الخلال في "علله" أن الإمام أحمد سئل عن هذا الحديث فقال: ما زلت منكرا له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r3.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim from Abu Dharr says the Prophet saw his Lord with his heart, not his eyes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: رآه بقلبه، ولم يره بعينه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r4.speaker: ابن خزيمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r4.claim: Ibn Khuzayma argues that the report is interrupted between Abdullah ibn Shaqiq and Abu Dharr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r4.anchor: وحاول ابن خزيمة أن يدعي انقطاعه بين عبد الله بن شقيق وبين أبي ذر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r5.speaker: ابن الجوزي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi proposes that Abu Dharr asked before the Night Journey, and that the Prophet would have affirmed the vision if asked afterward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r5.anchor: وأما ابن الجوزي فتأوله على أن أبا ذر لعله سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل الإسراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the timing explanation as very weak: Aisha asked after the Night Journey and was not told that the vision occurred; those who fault her are mistaken.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r6.anchor: وهذا ضعيف جدا، فإن عائشة أم المؤمنين، رضي الله عنها، قد سألت عن ذلك بعد الإسراء، ولم يثبت لها الرؤية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r7.speaker: ابن خزيمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says those who claim Aisha was addressed according to her understanding or was mistaken, including Ibn Khuzayma, are themselves mistaken.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452#2/r7.anchor: أو حاول تخطئتها فيما ذهبت إليه -كابن خزيمة في كتاب التوحيد (4) -، فإنه هو المخطئ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r1.claim: Al-Nasa'i transmits Abu Dharr's statement that the Prophet saw his Lord with his heart, but not with his eyesight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r1.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه بقلبه، ولم يره ببصره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra explains the second sighting in the verse as seeing Gabriel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال في قوله: {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} ، قال: رأى جبريل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r3.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet saw Gabriel in his original form twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى} قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل في صورته مرتين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r4.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r4.claim: Qatada and al-Rabi ibn Anas likewise say that the Prophet saw Gabriel in his original form twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r4.anchor: وكذا قال قتادة والربيع بن أنس، وغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود (على ظن محمد)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.claim: A report tentatively attributed to Ibn Masud says Muhammad saw Gabriel in his form twice: once when requested, when Gabriel filled the horizon, and again on the ascent. Gabriel then returned to his form and prostrated; the great signs were Gabriel's creation. Ahmad transmits it and Ibn Kathir calls it strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.anchor: قال محمد: أظنه عن ابن مسعود -أنه قال: إن محمدا لم ير جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين

JISHUMI:v9p6640/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r8.claim: Ruʾya is perception and can mean illusion, dream-conception in the heart, or knowledge in the heart, all by figurative extension.
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r8.anchor: ورؤية النوم: تصور واعتقاد بالقلب، ورؤية بالقلب وهو العلم

JISHUMI:v9p6640/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r10.claim: Nazla means one instance of descending.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r4.claim: Muhammad saw again, a second time, what he had seen on the first occasion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r4.anchor: يعني أنه رأى ما رآه ثانية بعد أولى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r5.speaker: كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r5.claim: Ka'b says God divided His speech and vision between Muhammad and Moses: Muhammad saw Him twice and Moses spoke with Him twice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p394/r5.anchor: قال كعب : إن الله تعالى قسم كلامه ورؤيته

MUQATIL:53:10-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:10-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:10-15/r3.claim: Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart another time.
MUQATIL:53:10-15/r3.anchor: رأى محمد صلىالله عليه وسلم ربه بقلبه مرة أخرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r1.anchor: ﴿ ولقد رآه ﴾ راى محمد جبريل عليهما السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r2.claim: “Once more” is explained through the construction taḍmīn; nazla is a noun of one occurrence and is accusative like the adverb “once.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r2.anchor: ﴿ نزلة أخرى ﴾ مرة لا تصح الا على مذهب التضمين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r3.claim: Gabriel descended again in his own form, and Muhammad saw him in that form on the Night of the Miʿrāj at al-Maʾwā.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#9/r3.anchor: اى نزل عليه جبريل عليه السلام نزلة اخرى في صورة نفسه فرآه عليها وذلك ليلة المعراج المأوى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.claim: Nazlatan is a verbal noun used circumstantially, meaning that he saw him descending another time.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.anchor: { نزلة } مصدر في موضع الحال كأنه قال: ولقد رآه نازلا نزلة أخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muḥammad saw his Lord with his heart a second time; Muslim transmits from Abū al-ʿĀliya that he saw Him with his heart twice.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: رأى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه مرة أخرى بقلبه. روى مسلم عن أبي العالية عنه قال: { ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى } { ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى } قال: رآه بفؤاده مرتين

QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r10.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās’s reading, “another descent” refers to Muḥammad, whose repeated ascents for the prescribed prayers each had a descent.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r10.anchor: فقوله: { نزلة أخرى } يعود إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنه كان له صعود ونزول مرارا بحسب أعداد الصلوات المفروضة، فلكل عرجة نزلة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Abū Hurayra identify the one seen on the second occasion as Gabriel; Muslim authenticates this report.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r12.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة في تفسير قوله تعالى: { ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى } أنه جبريل. ثبت هذا أيضا في صحيح مسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r13.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet saying he saw Gabriel in the highest horizon with six hundred wings, pearls and rubies scattering from his feathers.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:12-14/r13.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
